complexity.correctness_reason: On a skewed (linked-list-shaped) tree of more than about 1000 nodes — permitted once the 100-node cap is lifted — the recursion exceeds CPython's default recursion limit and raises RecursionError.
complexity.notes: There is an O(n) approach with O(n) time regardless of shape: a single bottom-up pass that ||returns each subtree's height and best diameter together, updating the answer as leftHeight + rightHeight at each node|| instead of rescanning subtrees. Stylistically, max(a, b, c) works directly on three arguments (no list needed), and the else after return is redundant. Recursion depth also becomes linear on skewed inputs, which is what trips the correctness limit below.
complexity.summary: Top-down recursion: at each node it computes the heights of both subtrees with a separate maxDepth call and takes the max of leftHeight + rightHeight against the diameters of the two subtrees. Heights are recomputed at every node, so total work is O(n * depth) — linearithmic on a balanced tree, quadratic on a skewed one.
